cells.date: Vikrama 1897, Śaka 1762, Uttarāyaṇa, Śisira-ritu, Phālguṇa su 5, Friday, Asvin= 1841 A D, February 26
cells.remarks: States that the royal headquarter was at Idara (Idar) Records that the construction and the consecration of a temple, for god Trivikrama, at the village of Muḍeṭi in the Idara praṅgaṇa (pargaṇa), was completed by Thākūra (i.e., Thākūra) Sūrajamalaji, Jālamasimhaji and a number of other persons Vijayarāma of the Sōmaparā-jñāti and Vṛimdāvana, son of Umēdarāma were the sculptors connected with this work Further, it refers to the making of a temple for Vishnu (perhaps this is a repeated reference to the temple mentioned above) and an image of Hanumān called Duḥkha-bham-jana Also states that a person named Vuvāmnadaḷajī cut off (his) hand for the sake of the temple Ends with a verse in Śārdūlavikrīḍita metre in praise of god Dāmodara

cells.remarks: Records an undertaking given by the tānattār of Māluvachakkaravattisvaramudaiya-nāya-ṉār of Uñjaṉai in Perumbūr-nāḍu in Kēraḷa-siṅga-vaḷanāḍu to Pompaṉ Chokkaṉār alias Tuvarāpativēḷār belonging to agapparivāram of Āṉaimuṉāṭṭavutta, an eastern hamlet of Śivallamaṅgalam which is again an eastern hamlet of Mēlkalakūṟu in respect of the dēvadāna lands in the village Chō[ḷa*]ṅkudikkāḍu alias Karuṇākaranallūr, which were once enjoyed by Māḍan Śīvalṅgappērumāḷ alias Kāṅgēyappichchar and Tiru-mēṉalaṅgyār as kudmiṅgā-kāṇi The lease on these lands was transferred to Śōḷamala-ippērumāḷ from the above mentioned two persons when they fail to fulfil the obligations and to pay even the fine (ḍeṇḍam) for the lapse, to the tānattār The dēvakanms, srīkāryam-cheyvārgal have agreed to collect and give the mēlvāram of 1/3-share, for the different crops raised in the aforesaid lands inclusive of the share to the shepherd (uḍaiyar) and to the deity, after exempting the taxes such as tirumāḍi, kōḷaṟai, mākkaṟṟai, tirunāl-tēvai, etc. A number of persons are stated to have attested the puḍipāḍu whuch was drafted by Kōyi-kanakkupillai In characters of the 14th century

cells.remarks: Records the grant of lands in Karaḍippāṛai alias Pāṛṛama-pāṇḍyanallūr, a western hamlet of Paimpōḷi-paṛṛu in Vaḍa-Āṛṇāḍu as tiruvaḍaiyāṭṭam by Tangachchvenru-mālayitta-perumāḷ to sthanattār of Kulaśēkharavinnagar-em-berumān temple at Sengōṭṭai, an eastern hamlet of Nallūr-paṛṛu in Ten-Āṛṇāḍu for conducting the repairs (jīrṇoddhāranam) in the above temples from upāna to stūpi and for the purpose of worship and food offerings to the deity Nāyanār and Nāchchiyār during the service called Śrīvallabhan-sandhi, after consercrating the images mentioned herein It it stipulated that the worship was to be conducted regularly by enjoying the lands along with other privileges as tiruvaḍaiyāṭṭam from this date The order was attested by Kirantūr-udayān In characters of the 16th century Published in T A S, Vol VII, part I, No 37, pp 55-56 and Proc of the second S I H C, pp 55-56

cells.location: BUDAUN
cells.place: Well adjacent to a mosque in Mamman Chauk Slab in the wall. Outside.
cells.remarks: Ikram ‘Alam Sahib, B.A., advocate of Budayun of Ihna ‘Ashari faith son of Maulavi Muhammad Katim ‘Alam Sahib Advocate, son of the chief Sadr-i-Jahan successor of Nawwab ‘Umdatul-Mulk (lit. Chosen of the empire) Diwan-i-Insha (Chancery of Correspondence) Malik Hamid-u-Din Sabzawat of Iran. The work was carried out at the instance of Maulana Nizami, Maulavi Diya Ahmad M.A. and Maulavi Tasadduq ‘Ali Sahib of Budayun. Caesarean well) in characters of about the 17th century.
